<main class="site-main"><section class="page-intro"><p class="section-number">Note · Evidence and belief</p><h1>Criteria move the answers. Separation moves discriminability.</h1><div class="article-meta"><span class="status">Published</span><span>updated 04 Sep 2026</span></div></section><article class="prose"><p>Suppose two groups of latent evidence sit on the same scale. A six-point rating asks where to place five cut-points. Those cut-points are criteria: they decide which category receives an observation.</p><p>Move the criteria and the response mix changes. A stricter rater can produce fewer high ratings without the underlying signal becoming any more or less separable.</p><blockquote>Criteria move the answers. Separation moves discriminability.</blockquote><h2>Why draw it?</h2><p>Ordinal models often arrive as coefficients and thresholds. Signal detection theory gives the same structure a picture: distributions for latent evidence, thresholds for response categories, and d′ for the distance between the distributions when variance is held equal.</p><p>The picture is a teaching device, not a publication estimate. It keeps one warning visible: changes in observed ratings are not automatically changes in sensitivity.</p><h2>Related project</h2><p><a class="text-link" href="../../experiments/ordinal-regression-viz/">See OrdinalRegressionViz</a> for the package, example figure, and project limits.</p></article></main>
